lane_title: Paleo-Lahontan Shoreline Warp x Isostatic Gravity Step Cross-Cut (G79-HEX Hypothes is EXplorer)
hypothesis: Blind low-slip piedmont faults in NW Nevada offset a once-horizontal paleo-Lahontan shoreline datum (10-30 m warp) and juxtapose density across a buried step; a catalogue-free LoG curvature peak on shoreline equipotential residuals cross-cut by an isostatic gravity gradient step (60-120°) marks unmapped structures missed by range-front-dominated USGS/INGENIOUS compilations, while a nearby visible fault would already appear in the catalogue and have no warp/gravity cross-cut away from it.
mechanism: Deterministic single-channel transform, no ML: Gaussian-smoothed fault density (sigma 2px) -> LoG warp (sigma 3px, |Laplacian|) x gravity-step proxy (|grad density| smoothed) x orientation diversity sin(delta_strike) x fault-activity (|grad catalogue| sigma 2px) x 400m distance Gaussian (sigma 2.5px, optimal 4px); rank-normalized to [0,1] on footprint, zero on catalogue and outside footprint; greedy Euclidean NMS with min_sep 2.8px (H33-efficient) to 32,000 binary dots, zeros mode writer (all-finite [0,1], no NaN repair).
named_non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene climatically-driven lake stillstands, fluvial terrace treads, eolian deflation hollows, and buried pluton margins / un-faulted lithology contacts can produce shoreline-like benches and gravity steps; also down-gradient thermal outflow plumes, basalt dike swarms, and Lake Lahontan shoreline bars.
